sections.heading: Java Custom Exception
paragraphs: The custom exception refers to the creation of your own exception to customize an exception according to the needs. The custom exceptions are derived from the Exception class.

sections.heading: Need of Java Custom Exceptions
paragraphs:
• To categorize the exceptions based on the different types of errors in your project.
• To allow application-level exception handling.

sections.heading: Create a Custom Exception in Java
paragraphs: To create a custom exception, you need to create a class that must be inherited from the Exception class.

sections.heading: Syntax
paragraphs: Here is the syntax to create a custom class in Java -
You just need to extend the predefined Exception class to create your own Exception. These are considered to be checked exceptions.

sections.heading: Rules to Create Custom Exception
paragraphs: Keep the following points in mind when writing your own exception classes −

• All exceptions must be a child of Throwable.
• If you want to write a checked exception that is automatically enforced by the Handle or Declare Rule, you need to extend the Exception class.
• If you want to write a runtime exception, you need to extend the RuntimeException class.
